lead.t: Inotropes/Vasopressors: If cardiogenic shock is present (hypotension despite fluid optimisation), consider inotropes (e.g., dobutamine) or vasopressors (e.g., norepinephrine) guided by haemodynamic status.

snip.t: Inotropes/Vasopressors: If cardiogenic shock is present (hypotension despite fluid optimisation), consider inotropes (e.g., dobutamine) or vasopressors (e.g., norepinephrine) guided by haemodynamic status.

An inotrope such as dobutamine is required to increase contractility and systemic perfusion, along with cautious diuresis; beta-blockers and vasodilators are contraindicated in the presence of acute hypotension and shock.
Inotropes: May be considered in severe right ventricular failure with cardiogenic shock (e.g., dobutamine) to improve cardiac output.
Stabilise septic shock with crystalloid fluid challenges guided by signs of fluid overload; initiate inotropes or vasopressors if refractory.
Start an inotrope (dobutamine) or an inodilator (milrinone) to restore forward flow, adding a vasopressor (noradrenaline) if profound hypotension coexists.
Irreversible (refractory) shock: Persistent hypotension and profound tissue hypoperfusion despite high-dose vasopressors, inotropes, and appropriate volume resuscitation.
Inotropes: Initiate dobutamine in cardiogenic shock with persistent hypoperfusion despite adequate intravascular filling pressures to improve myocardial contractility.
*Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT):* Preferred in hemodynamically unstable patients (e.g., septic shock on inotropes) or acute brain injury/cerebral oedema.
